notes:
Account snapshot: mid-size global fintech building a client-facing conversational assistant and embed-based search for transaction data. Evaluation centered on Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) + Private for regulated workloads. Key asks: throughput guarantees during market-open spikes, deterministic p95 latency for interactive chat, and clear SLA language for multi-region failover.

What they told us (paraphrase/highlights):
- "We need predictable tail latency during peak — p95 target <=150-200ms for short chat requests; can tolerate higher p99 for long context generations." — Head of Platform.
- Workload mix: ~65% short-turn chat (avg 120 tokens), 25% embeddings/semantic search, 10% long-form summarization rerank.
- Expected steady-state: 120 concurrent chat sessions per AZ (NA + EU), peak: 450 concurrent sessions across regions during market open. Estimate ~120k tokens/minute peak.
- Preferred instance types: A100/H100 family for LLMs; open to quantized variants if Redwood can guarantee latency SLOs.
- Failover model desired: active-active preferred, but procurement favors active-primary with cross-region automatic fallback to avoid double-cost. require at least 20-25% reserved headroom per region for failover bursts.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to smaller quantized model in same region if primary pool saturated, then cross-region if still constrained.
- Resiliency expectations: 99.95% regional availability SLA for dedicated pool; credits and clear RTO/RPO for zone failures. legal will redline uptime definitions.
- Data residency: EU data must stay in EU-resident pools for EU customers; NA data primarily in NA. encryption keys via customer KMS (bring-your-own).
- Security/compliance blockers: PCI-DSS scoping pending; need clear on audit log retention and SSO provisioning (SAML).

POC scope and Milestones:
- Load test (week 1): validate p95 latency at 80/100/120 GPU reservation configs.
- Failover run (week 2): simulate single-AZ outage, observe routing/fallback latency and session continuity.
- Cost/perf analysis (week 3): compare single region overprovision vs multi-region reserved pools with 20% headroom.
- SLA negotiation (ongoing): draft redlines: credit calc, maintenance windows, and clear definition of "region" vs "AZ" in SLA.

Pricing & procurement notes:
- Finance pushing for 12–24 month reserved commitment with quarterly usage true-up. want tiered discount table (committed-GPUs -> unit $/token).
- Concern: cross-region egress charges when failing over; asked for workbook modeling egress + compute tradeoffs.

Open action items:
- SE (Noah) to produce detailed reserved-pool sizing worksheet with per-AZ numbers + headroom calc (deliver 2025-03-06).
- AE (Maya) to prep draft SLA with suggested uptime targets and credit formulas; share with legal (2025-03-09).
- Request from customer: sample runbook for AZ failover and latency degradation thresholds.
